light_description: Early Sound Dog overdrive; later BLUE DOG EVO is explicitly described as its evolution.
Crunchier Sound Dog overdrive developed from study of TS and GT-OD style circuits.
FET-clipped overdrive designed for a warm, amp-like response.
High-gain overdrive using CMOS gain stages and diode clipping.
Evolution of WARM DOG with revised tone circuitry and a continuously variable COLOR control.
Evolution of BLUE DOG with COLOR control replacing the earlier tone-shift switch.
Sound Dog distortion with mode switching; later version changed tone control for selectable clipping.
Smaller companion to DACHS-TORTION using MOSFET clipping and a compact control set.
Sound Dog fuzz with J-FET/MOS-FET amplification and asymmetric clipping options documented for ver.2.
Core SPI overdrive documented as an original compact handmade model.
Natural overdrive developed with guitarist Toshio Miyawaki and later offered as a standalone SPI model.
Two-channel overdrive developed to Miyawaki's requirements, with Fender-like and fuller gain voices.
Nutube-based overdrive; SPI launched it as an early Nutube effects design.
Nutube overdrive developed from the Viper concept, combining a bufferless TS character with Nutube response.
SPI distortion that avoids conventional diode clipping and uses an LM386-derived gain stage for deep, articulate distortion.
Original SPI fuzz line documented in Guitar Magazine and SPI/retailer coverage.
2022 Kumamine collaboration distortion, developed and fully supervised by Soul Power Instruments.
2022 Kumamine collaboration overdrive with broad gain range and mid-focused drive/boost response.
2022 Kumamine collaboration fuzz explicitly developed as a transistor-flavored fuzz.
2022 Kumamine collaboration bass overdrive with clean-signal blending as gain increases.
Handmade distortion aimed at 1970s Marshall-style sound; high gain can clean up with playing dynamics.
Four-knob Sound Wave Lab overdrive documented in the TC Gakki catalog.
Marshall-oriented drive with selectable gain and clipping modes for a wide range of classic-to-modern voices.
Plexi/Marshall-style high-gain drive with VOLUME, GAIN, EQ and CHARACTER controls.
Tube-driven overdrive modeled on the Chandler Tube Driver concept and shown as a handmade Sound Wave Lab product.
Handmade fuzz emphasizing blendable effect and dry paths, with a Sound Wave Lab modification to preserve clarity.

light_description: Professional version of the representative Ultimate Drive, commercialized from a specification made for guitarist Daisuke Miyazaki.
Wide-range overdrive with two gain modes, clean blending and pre-distortion low-cut shaping.
Big Muff-based modern fuzz with LowCut and Boost controls, capable of both massive and more classic fuzz textures.
Overdrive co-developed with guitarist Takashi Masuzaki, with clean blending and selectable silicon/LED clipping.
Two-channel Nutube drive using internal voltage boosting and multi-stage tube gain rather than conventional clipping devices.
Two-channel pedal with independent overdrive and booster sections; a documented Watanabe Music 75th Anniversary edition exists.
Third STOMPROX product, a Japanese high-gain distortion with separate GAIN and DRIVE sections plus MID and TONE.
